title: Do Third-Party Web Traffic Estimates Preserve Causal Variation?
abstract: arXiv:2609.30481v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Researchers increasingly rely on third-party platforms such as Similarweb and Semrush to measure web traffic when first-party analytics are unavailable. Yet these platforms report model-generated estimates rather than raw data, raising questions about whether their measures preserve the temporal and cross-source variation required for causal inference. As a motivating diagnostic, we examine reported referral traffic around two documented search-engine outages; the absence of visible discontinuities illustrates why preservation of identifying variation cannot be taken for granted. We then characterize three mechanisms, within-source smoothing, cross-source leakage, and treatment-induced calibration error, through which platform processing can generate nonclassical outcome measurement error. Analytical results and a stylized difference-in-differences simulation show that this error can attenuate, amplify, or reverse estimated treatment eff

translated_title: 第三方网络流量估计能否保留因果变异？
translated_abstract: 当第一方分析数据不可用时，研究者日益依赖Similarweb和Semrush等第三方平台来测量网络流量。然而，这些平台报告的是模型生成的估计值而非原始数据，这引发了一个问题：它们的测量结果是否保留了因果推断所需的时间维度和跨来源变异。作为动机性诊断，我们考察了两次有记录的搜索引擎宕机事件前后报告的引荐流量；可见不连续性的缺失表明，识别性变异的保留不能被想当然地认定。随后，我们刻画了平台处理过程可能产生非经典结果测量误差的三种机制：来源内平滑、跨来源泄漏以及处理诱发的校准误差。分析结果和简化的双重差分模拟表明，这种测量误差可能削弱、放大甚至反转估计的处理效应。
tldr: 本研究揭示第三方网络流量估计因来源内平滑、跨来源泄漏和处理诱发校准误差三种机制产生非经典测量误差，可能削弱、放大甚至反转因果推断中的处理效应估计。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that third-party web traffic estimates can introduce nonclassical measurement error through within-source smoothing, cross-source leakage, and treatment-induced calibration error, potentially attenuating, amplifying, or reversing estimated treatment effects in causal inference.
